sections.counts:
Squat and bench counts hold up. Squat sets 3, 4 and 6 match your log exactly; sets 1, 2 and 5 show one extra cycle, which is the walk-out or re-rack, and the clean count is still 5, 4 and 5. Bench set 2 matches (10). Set 3 reads 10 for 8 logged and set 1 reads 9 for 10, so the bench counts are off by one or two either way.

The superset counts in your log are uncertain (you weren't sure of them), so for pulldown, pushdown, hammer curl and lateral raise the watch's count is the better estimate and the page shows no verdict against the log. The watch saw 6, 9 and 8 pulldowns (8, 8, 7 logged), 9, 10 and 9 pushdowns (10, 10, 8 logged), 10 and 6 hammer curls and 8 and 9 lateral raises (10 and 10 logged). The hammer curls are the most trustworthy of these: every one of the 16 curls is clean. The first pulldown at 70 kg is the least: only 4 of 6 cycles are clean. The lateral raise numbers may undercount a small, quick movement. Deadlift 100 kg reads 8 cycles with only 2 clean, because setup pulls before the first rep blur into the set. The 120 kg pulls are slow (about 5–6 s per rep) and only 3 and 4 of the 5 reps are clean. The bar hitting the floor shows up as 5 sharp spikes in each set, which is how those two sets were placed.
sections.velocity:
Squat best-rep speed fell steadily with load: 0.69, 0.66 and 0.58 m/s for the 60, 80 and 100 kg warm-ups, then 0.54 and 0.51 m/s for the first and last 110 kg sets. That fits RPE rising from 7 to 8. Set 5's 1.14 m/s peak is the re-rack cycle, not a rep. Bench at a fixed 60 kg is the clearest fatigue signal today: mean speed went 0.38 → 0.35 → 0.32 → 0.30 m/s while RPE went 6 → 7 → 9 → 9.5. Within the last set speed dropped 39%, the largest drop of the session.

Deadlift 60 kg moved at 0.48 m/s. The 120 kg velocity numbers (0.12 and 0.37 m/s) are not reliable, because at that speed the height filter only partly isolates each pull.
sections.load_velocity: Squat is the only lift with a usable load–velocity line today: 0.69 → 0.51 m/s from 60 to 110 kg, five loads, each step slower than the last. Bench was done at one load, so it gives fatigue information, not a profile. Deadlift has only two clean loads (60 kg at 0.50 m/s and 120 kg at 0.45 m/s best rep), which is too few to draw a line.
sections.classifier: Every exercise has now been seen on an earlier day except the plain triceps pushdown, which the system has only seen as Triceps Rope Pushdown. Squat, bench and the hammer curl are recognised from wrist orientation alone. Pulldown is the one to watch: the arm is overhead (gravity on +x) with very little wrist rotation, the same pose as bench but upright, and it was easy to confirm by eye in the trace.
sections.detection: The recording is complete (61 minutes, no gaps). Automatic placement got squats and bench right but missed three things, all corrected by hand. First, the second 120 kg deadlift (at 38½–39 min) was not found, and the first one was labelled as the last. Second, pulldown and pushdown were done as a superset, alternating, and so were hammer curls and lateral raises. The log lists them one exercise at a time, so the automatic order was wrong from the pulldowns on. Third, a rhythmic bout at 51–52 min with the arm hanging is not in the log and is left unlabelled.
sections.rest: Squat rests grew from 104 s after the first warm-up to 221–309 s between the 110 kg sets. Deadlift working sets got 250–278 s. Bench rests were short for a main lift (100–123 s), which fits the lighter weight and higher reps. In the supersets the gap between exercises was 10–43 s: pulldown → pushdown 10–30 s, pushdown → pulldown about 40 s. Hammer curl → lateral raise was 11–14 s.

signature_desc.Squat (Barbell): Wrist cocked back beside the shoulder with the bar on the back. Almost no rotation; a sharp down-up every 3–4 s.
signature_desc.Deadlift (Barbell): Arm hanging straight, gravity on −x. Each rep ends with a sharp spike as the bar touches the floor; 120 kg reps took 5–6 s.
signature_desc.Bench Press (Barbell): Forearm vertical, gravity fully on +x. Pure vertical travel, very little rotation, about 2.5 s per rep.
signature_desc.Lat Pulldown (Cable): Arm overhead, gravity on +x while standing or seated upright; small wrist ripple each pull.
signature_desc.Triceps Pushdown: Forearm swings from about horizontal to hanging; gravity on x sweeps from about +0.4 to −1 each rep.
signature_desc.Hammer Curl (Dumbbell): Forearm from hanging to upright: gravity on x flips from −1 to about +0.8 each curl.
signature_desc.Lateral Raise (Dumbbell): Arm swings out to the side: gravity moves between x and z in opposite directions, about 2.5 s per rep.
